question: Does an anonymous structural role, defined without semantic labels or future outcomes, condition a glyph's transferable consequence law, and can independently learned glyph and role factors reconstruct glyph-role combinations deliberately withheld from training beyond strong local n-gram baselines?

v8RationaleOnly.reason: V8 establishes that anonymous hierarchical graph structure can track preserved role, but its visual critical-edge observations are not occurrence roles in the Linear A inscription stream. V14 carries forward the methodological principle, not V8 role labels or graph observations.

v13RationaleOnly.reason: V13 rejects ordered pair identity as a stable missing law and rejects exact two-token history as the explanation, motivating a relational-role test.

provenance.claimClass: post-V13 mechanistic test on reused evaluation inscriptions
provenance.rule: All role definitions, eligibility, masked glyph-role cells, smoothing, n-gram order, role-switch substitutions, gates, and adjudication are frozen using V10 train plus the already-frozen V12 state map before holdout/control are made available to the evaluation job.

roleDefinition.name: anonymous recurrence-topology role
roleDefinition.surfaceCanonicalization: Within the six-item past-through-current window, every non-boundary glyph identity is replaced by its first-occurrence index; <DOC> and <LINE> remain typed boundaries. Actual glyph identities are not part of the role key.

matrixHoldout.unit: glyph x anonymous-role combination, globally across train inscriptions
matrixHoldout.maskRule: Among eligible combinations, mask exactly those whose SHA-256 of glyph + canonical role key has first 64 bits modulo 4 equal to 0. Mask selection uses support and structure only, never next-token outcomes.
matrixHoldout.fitExclusion: Every train prediction event belonging to a masked glyph-role cell is excluded from glyph, role, factorized, direct, and n-gram consequence estimation. The frozen V12 state map itself is not refit.
matrixHoldout.trainOnlyFeasibility: With the frozen role definition and support rules, train contains 27 deterministically masked glyph-role cells covering 387 prediction events. This was established from train only before evaluation lanes were opened.

models.state: Frozen V12 48-state anonymous incoming state S; current glyph remains excluded from state assignment.
models.stateOnly: P(y|S), estimated after masked-cell removal with hierarchical backoff to the global outcome distribution.
models.glyphOnly: P(y|S,g), estimated after masked-cell removal and smoothed to stateOnly.
models.roleOnlyLeaveGlyphOut: P(y|S,R,-g): the role consequence is estimated from train events occupying role R after subtracting every contribution from the glyph g being scored; it hierarchically backs off through role-only and state-only distributions.
models.factorized: F(y|S,g,R) proportional to glyphOnly(y|S,g) * roleOnlyLeaveGlyphOut(y|S,R,-g) / stateOnly(y|S). This is normalized over the frozen V12 outcome vocabulary.
models.directDiagnostic: P(y|S,g,R) on unmasked train cells, smoothed to F. It is diagnostic only and cannot rescue the matrix-completion gate.
models.ngramSelection: Three-fold anonymous-inscription-hash cross-validation on train only after masked target events are removed. Freeze the lowest-log-loss order, tie broken toward lower order.
models.ngramTraining: The n-gram sees literal mapped glyph identities and up to eight previous mapped stream items. It is trained on every available train target position except the deliberately masked glyph-role target events, so the local-sequence baseline is not intentionally starved.

generalRoleTransfer.comparison: factorized versus glyphOnly on every evaluation event whose role is in the frozen eligible-role inventory; role evidence for glyph g is always learned leave-glyph-out from other glyphs.
generalRoleTransfer.independentUnit: anonymous inscription mean log2 probability advantage

matrixCompletion.primaryPopulation: Evaluation events whose exact glyph-role combination was deliberately masked from every V14 consequence model during train fitting.
matrixCompletion.strongInterpretation: A pass means the consequence of a never-trained glyph-role combination can be reconstructed from independently learned glyph and structural-role factors, including against a literal local-sequence model trained with contexts up to order 8.

roleSwitchCounterfactual.selection: For a supported (S,g,R), choose R' != R observed with the same S and g. Both roles must have support >= 6, support ratio <= 2, and frozen factorized consequence kernels separated by TV >= 0.10. Minimize support-ratio distance, then maximize TV, then SHA-256 tie break.
roleSwitchCounterfactual.outcome: log2 F(observed y|S,g,R) - log2 F(observed y|S,g,R').

adjudication.structuralRoleConditionsGlyphOperationAn: General role transfer, matrix completion against glyph-only and role-only, matrix completion against the frozen best n-gram, and role-switch counterfactual all pass in both reused evaluation lanes.
adjudication.unseenRoleFactorCompositionWithoutCounte: General role transfer and all three matrix-completion comparisons pass in both reused lanes, but the frozen same-glyph role-switch counterfactual does not pass in both lanes.
adjudication.roleFactorTransfersButLocalSequenceSuffi: General role transfer and matrix factorization beat the one-factor baselines in both lanes, but the matrix factorization does not beat the frozen best n-gram in both lanes.
adjudication.roleSignalWithoutCompositionalMatrixTran: General leave-glyph-out role transfer passes in both lanes, but deliberately masked glyph-role cells are not reconstructed strongly enough in both lanes.
adjudication.noTransferableStructuralRoleConditioning: The leave-glyph-out structural-role factor does not pass the frozen transfer gates in both lanes.

positiveDoesSupport: an anonymous occurrence-level structural role that conditions glyph consequence prediction
cross-glyph transfer of the role effect because the role estimator excludes the glyph being scored
compositional reconstruction of deliberately unseen glyph-role combinations only if the matrix gate passes
structure beyond literal local sequence only if the frozen n-gram challenge passes
positiveDoesNotByItselfSupply: semantic names for the recovered roles

falsifiers.surfaceIdentityLeakageIntoRole: Abort if any actual glyph codepoint or transliteration is serialized into the role key rather than first-occurrence canonical indices and typed boundaries.
falsifiers.futureLeakage: Abort if the predicted next mapped token or any later token contributes to role assignment.
falsifiers.matrixLeakage: Abort if a masked glyph-role event contributes to V14 consequence estimation or n-gram target counts.
falsifiers.sameGlyphRoleLeakage: Role probabilities for a scored glyph must subtract all train contribution from that glyph, not only the masked cell.
falsifiers.evaluationLeakage: Abort if holdout/control participates in role eligibility, mask selection, n-gram order selection, role-switch selection, thresholds, or smoothing.
